messages.subject: R code for NUTS (the original Matlab link also doesn't seem to work in the paper)
parts:
Hello all,

I was hoping to write my own version of NUTS in R for students to play with. I looked at the original paper here: http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/research/unpublished/nuts.pdf but the link to the Matlab implementation doesn't seem to work. Does anyone have a copy of this?

Alternatively (and preferentially) has anyone written a version in R? If not, will share my version once done.

Best,

Ben

parts:
We've made a ton of progress on the algorithm since
the original paper, so even if you do manage to implement
the Hoffman and Gelman version, it won't match Stan's
implementation. In particular, there's better adaptation
and the slice sampling has been replaced with multinomial
sampling. See Michael Betancourt's arXiv papers and
the Stan code.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] R code for NUTS (the original Matlab link also doesn't seem to work in the paper)
parts:
How did you test it? NUTS is a very difficult algorithm to get
right because of the subtle steps required for detailed balance.
Off by one errors can lead to code that seems right, but leads
to slight bias in estimates.

Basic static HMC is only a few lines of code and gets across
the basic idea of how the Hamiltonian flow lets you move across
distributions in a single iteration.

- Bob

messages.author: 87d6a01c1ab6ddf0
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] R code for NUTS (the original Matlab link also doesn't seem to work in the paper)
parts: Following up on what Bob has said, I think it should be possible to replicate the Stan code itself in R. The variable naming convention in the code follows the paper to which Bob refers. I believe all you need is in `src/stan/mcmc/hmc/nuts/base_nuts.hpp` assuming you have a symplectic integrator available. I couldn't find any in R not even leapfrog :( but it is easy enough to implement.
